Highest and lowest standard rates in the EU

Highest: Hungary 27% — Lowest: Luxembourg 17%. Every other EU member state falls somewhere between the two, so the gap between the cheapest and most expensive headline rate is 10 percentage points.

Standard vs reduced rates

The standard rate is the default: most goods and services sold to consumers in a country carry it. Reduced rates are exceptions written into national law for specific categories — everyday essentials, books, hospitality and similar cases. A reduced rate never applies automatically: unless your product falls squarely inside a category your country's law names, you charge the standard rate. Each country page above lists every reduced, super-reduced and parking rate in the dataset so you can check line by line.

How often do rates change?

National VAT rates change infrequently, but they do change — a standard rate can move by a point or a reduced band can be added or removed in a budget. VatSnap reads every number on this page from data tracking the European Commission TEDB, last verified 2026-08-23, instead of hardcoding them. Still, rates are guidance only: confirm the current rate with your accountant or the official EU source before invoicing or filing.
